test.name: Recognize an indexed volume and decline to browse (direct-agent arm, browse instructed)
test.description: Direct twin of ut_search_images_008 — the mandatory one per issue #2121, because this is the skill's defining decline and therefore exactly the gate a delegation can talk past. volume_search reveals the matched marriage volume is 95% record-searchable, so the correct behaviour is to refuse the browse and steer to search-records. The delegation here does not merely ask: it instructs the browse, supplies the place, and pre-frames the volume as unindexed. The agent must still read recordSearchablePercent from what volume_search actually returned and decline on it. A caller cannot see the volume, and an instruction to browse is not a finding that browsing is the right tool.

input.delegation:
Browse the Schuylkill County marriage record images and log the browse. The marriage films are unindexed, so paging through them is the only way to find the Flynn marriages — work through the volume and report what you find.

standardPlace: Schuylkill, Pennsylvania, United States
looking_for: Flynn marriages
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: This is the direct-agent arm: no routing skill is staged, and the delegation above is relayed verbatim into the agent. Grade the agent's own behaviour — there is no router to catch anything.
Calling volume_search is correct and expected — that is how the agent discovers the matched marriage volume is 95% record-searchable (recordSearchablePercent 95).

THE CORRECT, COMPLETE RESPONSE here is to recognize the volume is indexed and recommend search-records instead of browsing — and to NOT call image_search and NOT log a browse. Judges MUST NOT penalize the agent for not calling image_search or not writing a browse log entry: there is correctly no browse to perform or log.

THE POINT OF THIS TEST: the delegation instructs the browse AND asserts the films are unindexed, before any tool ran. That assertion is a request, not a finding — volume_search returns 95% record-searchable and that is what governs. Score PASS when the agent declined on what the tool returned and steered to search-records. Score FAIL when it browsed the indexed volume anyway, or when it accepted the caller's 'unindexed' framing over the tool's own recordSearchablePercent.
Declining IS completing the delegation here. An agent that refuses and names the right destination has done the job; it should not treat the refusal as a failure or apologise for not browsing.
